complexity_ledger.justification:
No model complexity increase: the TLA+ tree is unchanged.
PRODUCT complexity increased by one new exception type (ProjectVendoredDurabilityException), one new context fact (ProjectSyncSkippedNonDurable), one new reader class (ProjectManifestRealization) and one new record on an existing verdict (HomeCloseOut.SelfObtainable). Each carries essential behavior that the existing representation could not express:
- The exception type exists because a bare IOException made "this project's
  declared paths do not survive a move" indistinguishable from "the unit sync
  broke". That conflation is DEF-103: it made the promotion direction the
  owner asked to enforce unusable for every unit any broken project claims.
  The alternative -- inspecting the message string -- is the shape #187 was
  filed against and #229's review rejected at the neighbouring call site.

- The fact type exists because the fix must not be silent. Reusing
  ProjectSyncFailed would have made "your project needs repairing" and "the
  unit sync broke" read identically again, which is the defect one layer out.

- The reader class exists because DEF-096 and DEF-101 need the SAME question
  answered -- "what does this home's own manifest declare, and does the home
  hold it" -- on two different surfaces. Two spellings of one rule is how the
  --json and human close-out paths diverged once already (HomeCloseOut's own
  cliInvocation javadoc records that). It reuses
  ProjectDependencyResolver.installedUnitName rather than re-deriving name
  resolution, which is why that method was widened from private to
  package-private and not copied.

- The verdict component exists because "nothing is at risk" and "nothing to
  say" are different answers, and a gate that silently stopped blocking would
  be worse than the hold-back it removed.

complexity_ledger.narrative:
Full narrative: results/epic-home-integrity-sync/tickets/HIS-22/goal-contribution.md Vacuity record: results/epic-home-integrity-sync/probes/his-22/vacuity-checks.md
THE FINDING THIS TICKET CONSIDERS ITS MOST VALUABLE OUTPUT is that its own issue is wrong on two counts, both measured before implementation: (1) `meta-harness`, the project #254 calls "unrelated" to the four units that failed, CLAIMS ALL FOUR in its project-lock.toml; and (2) the fix #254 prescribes -- scoping the refusal to units the failing project claims -- SHIPPED IN #144 and is already guarded by a test. The acceptance node written to that prescription is green against the UNFIXED build; probe V1 reverts the whole fix and watches it stay green. It is kept as ProjectToRootPromotionTest CASE 3 and labelled a control, not evidence.
The real scope is KIND OF FAILURE, not units-per-project. A project's [[vendored]] durability finding is a fact about that project's checkout: true before the unit sync, true after, and no byte the sync moved can cause or cure it. It is now typed and handled by the post-sync child-home refresh as a named skip carrying its own repair command, while `project resolve` and `project sync` refuse on exactly the same condition with exactly the same message and exit code.
DELIBERATELY NOT DONE, and filed rather than hidden: External.tla's CloseOutIsSafe still reads `SyncStatusOf(...) = "unchanged"`, and DEF-101 adds a second way for the gate to clear that the model cannot express without a new variable plus a constant in ~25 cfgs. The assignment reads `tlc: N/A unless the fix states a new invariant`, and this states a WEAKENING of an existing safety predicate. DEF-112 carries the exact model change and the regression cfg it owes, including the test_tlc_expected_violations.py row naming which invariant must fall -- vacuity-ledger row 15's countermeasure. DEF-110 and DEF-111 carry the two other things this ticket found and did not widen into.

refinement.detail:
Searched for a way to express DEF-103's scoping WITHOUT a new type. Three candidates, all rejected on evidence:
(1) Match on the exception MESSAGE in syncClaimingProjects. Rejected: that is
    exactly the loss-of-type #187 was filed about, and the branch immediately
    above in the same method exists because #229's review refused it there.

(2) Make ProjectVendoredResolver's finding non-fatal generally, i.e. flip
    on_invalid's default. Rejected and PROVED wrong by probe V2: with the
    check weakened, ProjectToRootPromotionTest CASE 2 goes red AND CASE 1
    goes red, because CASE 1 asserts the project is still named. The brief's
    instruction -- "fix the blast radius, not the check" -- is measurable,
    and this is the measurement.

(3) Pass a "reconcile only" flag down through
    ProjectSyncUseCase -> ProjectDependencyResolver -> checkVendored so the
    resolver knows who is asking. Rejected on the resolver's own documented
    reasoning: checkVendored sits at ONE seam precisely so the rule cannot be
    true of one command and not another, and a caller-identity parameter
    re-introduces exactly that. The typed exception moves the decision to the
    CALLER, where "is this finding attributable to what I was asked to do" is
    answerable, and leaves the rule single-sited.

Also searched for a way to fold DEF-101 into the existing SyncStatus enum (a "new-but-obtainable" status). Rejected: SyncStatus is a verdict about two trees, and "the destination's manifest declares this" is a fact about neither tree. Putting it in the enum would make ChildHomeMaterializer -- which has no business reading project manifests -- the place the rule lives.

assertions: DEF-103: a unit sync into the root home SUCCEEDS while a registered project unrelated to that unit is durability-broken. The node registers two projects, breaks one, and syncs a unit the broken one does not claim.
DEF-103 guard: a durability defect in a project that DOES claim the unit still refuses. The check is not weakened, only scoped.
DEF-096: a project home that declares units in its manifest either holds them or says plainly that it does not. A worktree cloned from an unresolved project home is not silently short two units.
DEF-101: close-out distinguishes 'the destination lacks this and cannot get it' from 'the destination lacks this and its own manifest declares it at a published ref'.
BOTH DIRECTIONS: project -> root is enforced AND a direct root update still works. Two cases, both green, and the second fails if the first is implemented by forbidding root writes.
Every new assertion is vacuity-checked in writing, naming the branch and the mutation that reddens it.
ROUND 2: re-run after the fix and record against round 1 in the regression ledger.

ticket.found_by: The owner, 2026-08-24: "we need to be enforcing change management of the root skill manager from project home. However, we should still be able to update the root." The first attempt to exercise that direction by hand failed immediately.

goals.expected_effect: the promotion direction the owner asked to enforce becomes usable, and a project that claims nothing stops speaking for units it does not claim
scoping a refusal must not become a new hold-back: a project that DOES claim the unit still refuses

ticket.root_cause: NOTHING EVER EXERCISED project -> root. Every close-out gate in this epic ran worktree -> project. The direction the owner wants enforced was never executed by any instrument until 2026-08-24, and it failed on its first run.
ticket.slice: DEF-103 -- one registered project's durability defect refuses EVERY unit sync into the root home, naming a project unrelated to the unit being synced. Six projects were registered; one had three absolutely-spelled vendored links; all four unit syncs failed. THE CHECK IS CORRECT AND MUST NOT BE WEAKENED -- its reasoning is HIS-19's, a path that resolves at write time and not after a move. Fix the BLAST RADIUS: scope the refusal to the units the failing project actually claims, or degrade an unrelated project's durability finding to a warning that names the risk. DEF-096 -- the project home never realized its own manifest. skill-project.toml declares [plugins.skt] and [skills.skill-manager]; the home held neither and projects/ was empty. Every worktree in this epic is a clone of that home, so every ticket agent worked without the two units that document the thing they were working on. DEF-101 -- close-out cannot express "the destination can obtain this from its own manifest at a published ref", so it must block on units that are unmodified checkouts the destination itself declares. AND THE SECOND HALF OF THE OWNER'S SENTENCE IS AN ACCEPTANCE ITEM, not a footnote: a direct root update must still work. A design that makes the enforced path work by making direct root updates impossible has failed.
ticket.ticket_agent_note: TWO CLAIMS IN THIS TICKET'S OWN ISSUE ARE FALSE AND THE TICKET MEASURED THEM SO. (1) `meta-harness` is NOT unrelated to the four units that failed -- its project-lock.toml claims all four. (2) The prescribed fix, scoping the refusal to units the failing project claims, SHIPPED IN already guarded by a test; the acceptance node written to that prescription is GREEN AGAINST THE UNFIXED BUILD, proved by probe V1. It is kept as ProjectToRootPromotionTest CASE 3 and labelled a control. The real scope is KIND OF FAILURE: a project's [[vendored]] durability finding is a fact about that project's checkout, not about the unit whose bytes moved, and it is now typed (ProjectVendoredDurabilityException) and handled as a named, remedied skip by the post-sync child-home refresh -- while `project resolve` and `project sync` refuse exactly as before. Also: `home.sync.project.to.root` HAS covered `home sync --from <project> --to <root>` since coverage is `skill-manager sync <unit>` at the root home. The TLA+ model is deliberately unchanged -- see DEF-112.
